label: 74HC595 8-bit Serial-In/Parallel-Out Shift Register with Output Latch

semantics.notes: Two-stage register: internal 8-bit shift register clocked by SHCP (shift clock) and an output latch clocked by STCP (storage/latch clock). DS=serial data input; /MR=async reset of shift register only (NOT the output latch); /OE=tri-state output enable. Typical use: shift 8 bits via SHCP, then pulse STCP to transfer to outputs. Q7S is the serial output for daisy-chaining. clockInputId=shcp — timing detection only on shift clock. STCP is a second independent clock not covered by clockInputId.

exportSupport.verilogNotes: Two always blocks: one for SHCP (shift clock), one for STCP (latch clock). /MR handled async in SHCP block. /OE handled by assign on outputs. Q7S driven by assign from internal shift register MSB.
exportSupport.vhdlNotes: Two processes for SHCP and STCP. Concurrent assign for Q7S and /OE.

testability.notes: Full test sequence: 1) /MR=0→reset shift register; 2) shift 8 bits via DS+SHCP; 3) verify outputs NOT yet updated (still old value in output latch); 4) pulse STCP to transfer; 5) verify Q[7:0] matches shifted bits; 6) test Q7S serial output appears at correct clock; 7) test /OE=1→Hi-Z outputs; 8) daisy-chain test: Q7S of first → DS of second.

risks.description: Two independent clocks (SHCP and STCP). clockInputId=shcp only. STCP timing violations are not detected by the race condition engine.
/MR resets the shift register but NOT the output latch. This is a common misunderstanding. Verify that the implementation correctly keeps output latch unchanged when /MR=0.
stateKeys=['q0'..'q7'] represent the OUTPUT LATCH, not the internal shift register. The internal shift register state is an implementation detail not exposed to STT.

modelLimits: Internal shift register not exposed as user-visible state (not in stateKeys).
Power-on: output latch Q[7:0]=0, internal shift register=0.
